questions.prompt: For Fe3+(aq) + SCN−(aq) ⇌ FeSCN2+(aq), only the complex contributes appreciably to red absorbance at the chosen wavelength. A small amount of concentrated SCN− solution is added with negligible volume change. What is expected after re-equilibration?
options: The red absorbance decreases because added reactant consumes the complex.
All Fe3+ must disappear completely.
The red absorbance increases as additional complex forms.
No change is possible because the original solution was at equilibrium.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Adding a reactant favors net consumption of some added SCN− and formation of more absorbing complex. A is incorrect: net forward reaction forms rather than consumes the complex. B is incorrect: a finite equilibrium constant does not imply complete consumption. D is incorrect: a composition disturbance can shift an equilibrium.

questions.prompt: For N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g), some NH3 is selectively removed at constant temperature and volume. What chemical response follows?
options: Net forward reaction produces additional NH3.
Net reverse reaction produces more N2 and H2.
K decreases because NH3 was removed.
The reverse reaction permanently stops.
questions.explanation: A is correct. Removing product favors its replacement through forward conversion of reactants. B is incorrect: that would consume the depleted product further. C is incorrect: composition changes do not change K at fixed temperature. D is incorrect: both directions can continue as the system re-equilibrates.

questions.prompt: A closed isothermal N2O4(g) ⇌ 2NO2(g) mixture at equilibrium is compressed. Which change in equilibrium composition is favored by the pressure increase?
options: A larger fraction must be NO2.
A larger fraction of the nitrogen-containing gas molecules is N2O4.
The dissociation equilibrium constant increases.
Both gases are completely consumed.
questions.explanation: B is correct. The side with fewer gas molecules is favored, so net association forms more N2O4. A is incorrect: the right side has more gas molecules and is disfavored by compression. C is incorrect: temperature is unchanged. D is incorrect: association conserves nitrogen and oxygen; it cannot remove all gas.

questions.prompt: Helium is added to an ideal reacting gas mixture at equilibrium while temperature and container volume are fixed. Helium does not react. What happens to the equilibrium composition?
options: It always shifts toward fewer gas molecules.
It always shifts toward more gas molecules.
K changes in proportion to total pressure.
It remains unchanged because reacting-gas partial pressures are unchanged.
questions.explanation: D is correct. Added helium increases total pressure but does not change nRT/V for any reacting gas. A is incorrect: total-pressure increase from inert gas at fixed volume does not compress the reacting gases. B is incorrect: their partial pressures have not decreased. C is incorrect: K is unchanged at fixed temperature.

questions.prompt: N2O4(g) ⇌ 2NO2(g) is endothermic in the forward direction. NO2 is brown and N2O4 is nearly colorless. A rigid sealed equilibrium vessel is heated. What compositional response is expected?
options: Net dissociation forms more NO2, strengthening its brown absorbance.
More N2O4 forms because heating favors every association reaction.
The brown color must disappear because particles move faster.
Composition cannot change because no material enters.
questions.explanation: A is correct. Heating favors the endothermic direction; more NO2 forms at fixed volume. B is incorrect: the specified forward direction absorbs heat. C is incorrect: speed alone does not remove the absorbing species. D is incorrect: a closed system can change its internal chemical composition.

questions.prompt: The forward synthesis N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g) is exothermic. At fixed volume, cooling an equilibrium mixture favors which change in composition?
options: More N2 and H2 are formed because cooling always favors dissociation.
K must remain exactly unchanged because volume is fixed.
More NH3 is formed as the heat-releasing direction is favored.
All molecular collisions cease.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Cooling favors the exothermic direction, increasing the equilibrium extent of ammonia formation. A is incorrect: the direction depends on enthalpy, not a universal dissociation rule. B is incorrect: temperature changes can change K. D is incorrect: thermal motion persists at ordinary lower temperatures.

questions.prompt: For A(aq) + B(aq) ⇌ C(aq), a dilute equilibrium solution is diluted with water at constant temperature. No side reactions occur. What net chemical response is favored?
options: A and B combine to make more C.
K becomes smaller because concentrations decrease.
All C must dissociate regardless of K.
Some C dissociates into A and B.
questions.explanation: D is correct. Dilution favors the side with more dissolved solute particles, here two on the reactant side. A is incorrect: that favors fewer solute particles, opposite to the dilution response. B is incorrect: K remains fixed at constant temperature. C is incorrect: a shift does not imply complete conversion.

questions.prompt: A catalyst is added without changing temperature, volume, or composition to an equilibrium gas mixture. What happens to the equilibrium amounts?
options: Products necessarily increase because only the forward path is catalyzed.
They remain unchanged, although both opposing reactions can become faster.
Reactants necessarily increase.
K increases because the activation barrier decreases.
questions.explanation: B is correct. A catalyst changes the approach kinetics without changing equilibrium position at fixed temperature. A is incorrect: a catalyst also provides a reverse path and cannot alter equilibrium favorability. C is incorrect: there is no imposed composition disturbance favoring that direction. D is incorrect: barriers control rates, not the equilibrium constant.

questions.prompt: At fixed temperature, CaCO3(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO2(g) is at equilibrium with both solids present. More pure CaCO3 is added without changing gas volume. What happens to equilibrium PCO2?
options: It doubles if the solid mass doubles.
It falls to zero.
It increases because K increases with the number of solid particles.
It remains unchanged.
questions.explanation: D is correct. Adding more of an already present pure solid does not change its activity or the equilibrium gas pressure. A is incorrect: pure-solid mass is absent from the expression. B is incorrect: the disturbance does not remove CO2. C is incorrect: K is unchanged at fixed temperature.

questions.prompt: For H2(g) + I2(g) ⇌ 2HI(g), all gases behave ideally. What compositional response is favored by an isothermal compression of an equilibrium mixture?
options: No net shift, because both sides have the same total gas coefficient.
A shift right because every compression favors products.
A shift left because there are two named reactant species.
A shift right because K becomes larger.
questions.explanation: A is correct. All reacting partial pressures scale together and the equal gas coefficients leave the equilibrium ratio unchanged. B is incorrect: the response depends on relative gas molecule counts. C is incorrect: gas stoichiometric totals, not the number of species names, determine this effect. D is incorrect: isothermal compression does not change K.

questions.prompt: In A ⇌ B at fixed temperature and volume, a small amount of A is added to an equilibrium mixture. Which description correctly limits the compensating response?
options: Every added A must disappear to recover the exact original amounts.
No B can form because B was already present.
Some added A converts to B; equilibrium does not require the added A to be completely removed.
The reaction becomes permanently irreversible.
questions.explanation: C is correct. A disturbance is partly counteracted until the equilibrium ratio is restored; final amounts can differ from the original ones. A is incorrect: Le Châtelier response does not demand restoration of the original amounts. B is incorrect: existing product does not prevent a net forward response. D is incorrect: a concentration change does not eliminate the reverse process.
